classification.difficultyReason: Direct recognition or a familiar short procedure. The input lies strictly between consecutive integers 1 and 2.

content.prompt:
Let $x\in\mathbb R$ and define $\lfloor x\rfloor$ and $\lceil x\rceil$ by
$$\begin{aligned}\lfloor x\rfloor&=\max\{m\in\mathbb Z\text{ where }m\le x\}\\\lceil x\rceil&=\min\{m\in\mathbb Z\text{ where }m\ge x\}\end{aligned}$$
These are respectively called the $\mathit{floor}$ and $\mathit{ceiling}$ of $x$. Find the value of $\lfloor\sqrt2\rfloor$.

answer.worked: $1<\sqrt2<2$, so the greatest integer no greater than $\sqrt2$ is $1$. Hence $\lfloor\sqrt2\rfloor=1$.
